system_prompt_style.evidence_quote: given the column candidates, current indexes, total storage budget, and budget already used, the planning agent first evaluates the stop criteria
system_prompt_style.note: Paper only; agent prompts filled with per-step inputs (Figure 2). Mechanism not shown in code.

env_context_strategy.evidence_quote: our approach extracts only index-relevant information and reorganizes it at the column level, merging all workload details associated with each database column to construct a compact set of indexable candidates
env_context_strategy.note: Closest value: a precomputed column-candidate summary of the workload is injected up front; no navigation tools.

context_compaction.note: Paper only; no config or run-loop code available. Workload summarization is input design, not history compaction.

observation_format.evidence_quote: We design a novel textual workload representation that transforms the complex index recommendation problem into an LLM-compatible format.

tool_call_format.note: Agents output action names ('Selection', 'Combination', 'Revision', 'Stop'), but the parsing format is not described; no code.

tool_count.note: No tools in the tool-calling sense; planner chooses among 3 low-level agents plus Stop.

edit_primitive.note: Not a file-editing system; no tool registry available.

protocol_standardization.note: Paper only; no dependency list to grep.

loop_primitives.evidence_quote: the planning agent first evaluates the stop criteria. If these criteria are not met, it outputs an action for the current sub-step: ‘Selection’, ‘Combination’, or ‘Revision’, each invoking a corresponding low-level agent.
loop_primitives.note: Algorithm 1 loop: plan step, execute low-level agent, reflect; revision agent removes regressive indexes.

planning_granularity.evidence_quote: Our method utilizes high-level agents to control the index selection process and low-level agents to select and revise indexes.
planning_granularity.note: Plan is per-step next-action choice with delegation to low-level agents.

multi_agent_topology.evidence_quote: The planning agent plays an important role in the multi-agent pipeline for managing problem sub-steps and determining which Low-level agents to deploy at each step.
multi_agent_topology.note: Paper calls it hierarchical (high-level planning+reflection, low-level workers); only one orchestration level, so orchestrator_workers.

delegation_mechanism.evidence_quote: it outputs an action for the current sub-step: ‘Selection’, ‘Combination’, or ‘Revision’, each invoking a corresponding low-level agent.
delegation_mechanism.note: Implementation of invocation not shown; role_handoff chosen as closest.

short_term_state.evidence_quote: Previous indexes selected Column candidates left Total budget Budget used
short_term_state.note: Algorithm 1 tracks I_a, B_a, Actions list.

long_term_memory.note: Static expert rules/external knowledge are prompt content, not cross-run memory.

self_verification.evidence_quote: a reflection agent is introduced to evaluate the current path, with the goal of identifying and correcting errors.
self_verification.note: Also a trained MLP regression indicator scores indexes for the revision agent (not an LLM judge).

retry_policy.evidence_quote: Output the final index selection𝐼 𝑎
retry_policy.note: Algorithm 1 runs a single loop and outputs once; no task-level retries.

rollback.note: Revision agent removes indexes but no rollback mechanism described.

cost_controls.evidence_quote: we introduce a hyperparameter𝛼, which defines the maximum number of planning sub-steps.
cost_controls.note: Only a step cap limits spend; storage budget is task constraint, not cost control. Closest value.

execution_isolation.note: Experiments on an isolated server; harness execution boundary not described.

tracing.note: Figure 6 shows a reasoning trace but logging mechanism not described.

eval_hooks.note: No repo; paper evaluates on TPC-H/TPC-DS/DSB/JOB.

guardrails.note: Revision agent hallucination check is task-level, not a guardrail.

target_domain.evidence_quote: we propose AMAZe, a zero-shot LLM-based index advisor with a multi-agent framework.

model_agnostic.evidence_quote: we adopt an API GPT-3.5-turbo [6], and three open-source LLMs, namely Qwen3-32b [42], Qwen3-14b and DeepCoder-14b [23].
model_agnostic.note: Default backbone GPT-4o-0806; abstraction layer not described.

primary_artifact.evidence_quote: AMAZe: A Multi-Agent Zero-shot Index Advisor for Relational Databases

first_release_date.note: Evidence shows arXiv v2 16 Sep 2025 only; v1 date not in evidence.
